scenes.vo: Lifecycle: create to sign to broadcast to mempool (waiting) to included in a block to confirmed to final. Ethereum the price has a base fee (burned) plus a priority tip (to get included sooner). Gas price is quoted in gwei (1 gwei = 0.000000001 ETH). low-nonce transaction blocks all later ones until it confirms or is replaced (same nonce, higher fee). reversed. It differs by chain, and layer twos have their own rules (Module 5). Gas is the unit of computation. Cost = gas used times gas price. On Nonce: each account's transactions are numbered in order. A stuck Failed transactions still cost gas. The network did the computation even though the result was reverted. Finality: the point after which a transaction can't realistically be Explorers (for example Etherscan) show status, fee, sender, contract called, token transfers and logs.

scenes.vo: A swap uses 150,000 gas at 20 gwei: 150,000 times 20 = 3,000,000 gwei = 0.003 ETH. At $3,000/ETH that's $9. The same swap during congestion at 80 gwei costs $36. If you're compounding $1.50 of rewards, the gas costs more than the rewards. That's why position size matters on-chain.
scenes.cap: A swap uses 150,000 gas at 20 gwei: 150,000 × 20 = 3,000,000 gwei = 0.003 ETH. At $3,000/ETH that's $9. The same swap during congestion at 80 gwei costs $36. If you're compounding $1.50 of rewards, the gas costs more than the rewards. That's why position size matters on-chain.

lines: Your transaction reverted. Did you pay?
scenes.sub: Answer: Yes, for the gas used up to the point of failure.

lines: Why are your newer transactions all pending?
scenes.sub: Answer: An earlier nonce is stuck. Replace or speed it up, and the rest follow.
